payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Its confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. An independent audit retracted the earlier cycle-life claim; the governing corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.
